findings: Adult and phone oblique views retain palm and finger midtones with less pale washout.
Side views distinguish the raised fingers, heel contact and two-hand stack.
Contrast oblique and side views show internal hand boundaries, with the nails still marking the dorsal surface.
Phone child and infant hands fit the close-ups without clipped fingers or wrists.
Independent review found no large dark gaps or falsely disconnected wrists.
limits: Fine contour lines and existing joint seams can appear dotted at phone resolution.
Screenshots use local Chromium with software WebGL; this pass does not remodel the hands or mannequin.

diagnostics: The first surface-browser run used a canvas selector where glPixels expects a container. The helper appended a second canvas selector and returned null. The corrected fixture uses #wrap; production code and pixel assertions were unchanged.

One adult keyboard check issued ArrowLeft after a canvas-only photograph without verifying restored visibility and focus. The diagnostic passed with explicit visibility/focus checks. The final fixture also waits for two restored frames before exercising the same keyboard assertion; production camera code was unchanged.
